https://telex.hu/after/2026/08/06/heaven.text: Menü Kereső Heaven Street Seven: A krézi srácot az Emergency House-nak köszönhetjük After Sajó Dávid „Időnként ezek a dalok megérdemlik, hogy elhangozzanak” – indokolta adásunkban Szűcs Krisztián, hogy miért állt össze pár koncertre idén a 2015-ben feloszlott Heaven Street Seven (HS7). A Budapest Parkban tartott koncertjére készülő zenekar frontembere és dalszövegírója mellett a HS7 billentyűse és producere, Takács-Brouwer Zoltán Jappán volt a vendégünk. Szerinte a júliusi orfűi fellépésük a becsúszó hibák ellenére nem öregfiúk koncert volt, a dalok ugyanúgy működtek. Az eleinte angol nyelvű számokat megjelentető Heaven Street Seven a kilencvenes években az indie- és britpop zenék kedvelőit érte el, Szűcs szerint ez akkor kb. háromszáz embert jelentett Magyarországon. A már kizárólag magyar nyelvű dalokat tartalmazó, a 100 legfontosabb magyar lemez közé is beszavazott Cukor című lemezükkel azonban kitörtek ebből a buborékból. Arról a 2000-ben megjelent lemezről több dal, például a Mozdulj (ennek a klipjében szerepelt Marsi Anikó) és a Sajnálom is népszerű lett szélesebb körben, a Hol van az a krézi srác? -ot pedig döbbenetes módon még a Danubius rádió is játszotta, igaz, a szerkesztők ki akarták szedetni a tudja a halál sort a dalszövegből, amihez a zenekar nem járult hozzá. Szűcs arról is beszélt az adásban, hogyan inspirálta a szintén újra aktív Emergency House a legnagyobb slágerük szövegét. A HS7 tagjai sokáig hittek abban, hogy egy rendszeresen Nyugat-Európában turnézó, külföldön is elismert produkcióvá nőhetik ki magukat, ehhez egy ponton elég közel is álltak, de ahogy Szűcs fogalmazott, a magyar rock ‘n’ roll ugarnak azért vicces és nyomorult dolgai is voltak, így ez az álom elúszott. 2006-ban nagyjából 600 jelentkező együttesből ők kapták az European Breakthrough Awardot, ami azt jelentette, hogy az EU-hoz akkoriban csatlakozó országok zenekarai közül leginkább bennük látta az európai szakma a nemzetközi áttörés lehetőségét. Később a kultzenekarnak számító Churchcsel volt közös turnéjuk, így több száz ember előtt játszottak például Londonban. Utólag a zenekar úgy látja, ez az időszak elszalasztott lehetőség volt, a magyar szakmai szereplők ugyanis nem tettek igazán semmit azért, hogy a HS7-nek tényleg összejöjjön a nemzetközi siker. Cannes-ban már a MIDEM zenei konferencián is látszott, hogy a zenekar ügyét nem veszik komolyan a hazai szereplők, így esély sem volt arra, hogy Yonderboihoz hasonló karriert fussanak be külföldön. Szűcs szerint ebben az sem segített, hogy a HS7 – Robert Musil regényét idézve – úgynevezett tulajdonságok nélküli zenekar volt, nem volt könnyen megjegyezhető háttérsztorijuk, imidzsük, amivel könnyebben el lehetett volna adni a zenéjüket. „Ha én vagyok a világ legjobb biciklise, és kapok egy biciklit, akkor sem fogom utolérni a Trabantot” – mondta Szűcs, utalva ezzel arra, hogy Magyarországról sokkal több pénz, szakértelem és energia kellett volna ahhoz, hogy versenybe tudjanak szállni egy hasonló kvalitású nyugat-európai zenekarral. A zenekar két tagja szerint a Cukor után a Tudom, hogy szeretsz titokban volt a másik esszenciális HS7-lemez, az azt követő, befejezetlennek ható Jazz az útkeresésről szólt, az életművet lezáró, 2012-ben kiadott Felkeltem a reggelt pedig már inkább Szűcs és Jappán közös munkájának tekinthető. A zenekar az utolsó lemez idejére megrekedt, elfáradt, Jappán szerint végül egy megalázó, halászléfesztiválos fellépés után érezte azt, hogy ennek a történetnek vége, nincs értelme tovább csinálni. A HS7 végül 2015-ben jelentette be a feloszlását. A nemrég novelláskötettel ( Utazás a kegyetlenbe ) jelentkező Szűcs a műsorban arról is beszélt, hogy a HS7 nem lesz üzemszerűen működő zenekar, nem írnak új dalokat, ez egy pár koncertre szóló összeállás. Jappán pedig elárulta, hogy felmerült egyszer komolyabban, hogy összeálljon a másik zenekara, a Soerii & Poolek, de jelenleg kevés esélyt lát arra, hogy a Beton.Hofi zenekarában játszó Kovács Gergellyel közös produkciójukat megint színpadra vigyék. http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/17/at-le.text: At least seven people have been killed and more than a dozen injured in a stampede at a Hindu temple in India's eastern state of Bihar.The crush happened at the Ashok Dham temple in Lakhisarai district early on Monday as thousands of worshippers gathered to make offerings to the Hindu deity Shiva during the holy month of Shravan.District magistrate Shailendra Kumar told AFP that panic broke out after rumours spread that an electricity pole had fallen on devotees inside the temple grounds.Other reports suggested fears of electrocution contributed to the panic, while Kumar said the arrival of two trains within a short period had caused the number of worshippers at the temple to surge. A section of barricading subsequently collapsed as people attempted to escape."The situation is under control now," Kumar told AFP, putting the number of injured at 19.Local reports said many of those caught in the crush were women, with at least four of those killed identified as women aged between 44 and 55.Bihar's Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary described the deaths as "heart-wrenching" and announced compensation of 400,000 rupees ($4,180) for the family of each person killed. State minister Vijay Kumar Sinha said the circumstances surrounding the disaster would be investigated.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also expressed his condolences to the victims' families and said local authorities were assisting those affected.Deadly crowd crushes have repeatedly occurred at large religious gatherings in India, where huge numbers of worshippers can place severe pressure on crowd-control measures.More than 120 people were killed at a religious gathering in Uttar Pradesh in 2024, one of India's deadliest crowd disasters in recent years.

http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/23/trump.text: US President Donald Trump has renewed his proposal on the future of the Strait of Hormuz, after posting on the Truth Social platform a map that depicts the strategic waterway as "new American territory", though he did not comment on the image.This is not the first time Trump has published the same map highlighting the Strait of Hormuz, as he had already shared it on 18 August.The US president first floated the idea of treating the strait as American territory on 15 August."After we finish defeating Iran, which is suffering a very severe defeat, I will soon announce that the Strait of Hormuz will be land belonging to the United States," Trump said at a rally in New York.The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important shipping lanes; before the outbreak of the war, around one-fifth of global exports of crude oil and liquefied natural gas passed through it.While Iran insists it has asserted control over the strait, Trump, for his part, maintains that the United States is the one that "fully controls" the passage.Tehran has kept the strait closed since the war began, and its dispute with Washington continues over the conditions for reopening it.In a related development, an official Iranian account earlier described the US state of California as "new land belonging to Iran".Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi also joined the response to Trump's remarks, writing: "His illusions about the Strait of Hormuz will be corrected soon, or we will correct the illusions of this delusional man."Tehran ties reopening Hormuz to 'changing US behaviour'Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on Saturday that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the United States fulfils its commitments and changes what he called its "behaviour"."The Strait of Hormuz is closed, despite American claims, and it will not be opened until America corrects its behaviour... This time, America must first honour its commitments," Rezaei told Iranian state television.Iran warns Gulf states not to join Washington's sanctionsRezaei issued a warning to countries that might join US economic measures against Tehran."We declare to all countries... Do not join the economic war being waged by the United States," he said, stressing that "any country that takes part in imposing economic restrictions on us will be considered an enemy."The Iranian official also threatened to "harm" the interests of countries that, in his words, "refuse to distance themselves" from the United States.Rezaei said Iran has so far used only part of its capabilities, noting that the attacks it has carried out have targeted US military bases only, without hitting the United States' economic interests."So far, we have targeted military bases only, but if they want to impose economic sanctions on us, the United States has oil companies and other businesses around Iran and elsewhere, and we will strike them," he added:Rezaei warned President Trump that any new move against Iran could trigger a major escalation.Tehran and Washington signed a memorandum of understanding in June aimed at ending the war and paving the way for a broader agreement between the two sides.However, the process of reaching an understanding later stalled because of disagreements over how it should be implemented, as well as disputes surrounding navigation arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz.Talks involving Iran and the Sultanate of Oman on regulating traffic in the vital waterway have continued, but have so far failed to produce a breakthrough or a decisive agreement.

https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: People rescued from the dinghy were supported by emergency services in Calais. Photograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen People rescued from the dinghy were supported by emergency services in Calais. Photograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images Immigration and asylum Three people dead, including a child, in attempt to cross Channel to UK Official says deaths – and dozens of injuries – were probably caused by crushing on boat carrying 105 people Rajeev Syal and agencies Mon 28 Sep 2026 07.45 EDT First published on Mon 28 Sep 2026 06.40 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 10-year-old child and two women died ⁠attempting ​to cross the Channel on Monday, French authorities have said. Their deaths and the injuries of dozens of others in a large dinghy were probably caused by crushing, according to a French official. France’s maritime ​police ‌said ‌they received a ‌distress call in the early hours from an inflatable dinghy carrying 105 people that had ‌run into trouble in calm seas. The three passengers were treated onboard but were later confirmed dead by an emergency medical team flown out by helicopter. François-Xavier Lauch, the prefect of Pas-de-Calais, told a press conference: “Apparently there was no drowning, it was likely crushing – which is just as dreadful, especially if we think of the 10-year-old child.” The incident happened off the coast of Wissant, a village about 14 miles (23km) from Calais. A spokesperson for the local prefecture confirmed “a provisional total of three deaths and many more injured”, adding that “sea conditions were calm – the weather is good”. The prefecture described the boat as a “water taxi”, saying it had arrived relatively empty from an inland waterway before picking up passengers from the beach at Wissant. At 10.30am local time (9.30am UK time) six rescue boats were still at the scene searching for people in the water. At least 17 people, including women and children, have died in the Channel this year while attempting to reach the UK. Many have drowned, while others have died in incidents involving overcrowded boats. Three bodies were found last week after chaotic “water taxi” departures of this kind in northern France. So far this year, 18,609 people have made the Channel crossing – more than 40% fewer than at the same point last year. The number is also more than 25% lower than at this stage in 2024, when 25,165 people had crossed the Channel. Last week there were two uncontrolled landings in the UK, where dinghies arrived without being intercepted by authorities. It comes as more than 80 people, including a baby, are feared to have died while attempting to reach Spain’s Canary Islands by sea in August. On Monday, a rescue boat arrived at the port of Calais in the mid-morning, where it began disembarking people rescued from the accident. A coach, fire service and police vehicles were deployed at the scene. The northern beaches of France have become a key crossing point for people without visas hoping to cross the Channel. They pay people smugglers to board unstable rubber dinghies to make the journey across one of the world’s busiest shipping routes. At least 29 people lost their lives last year trying to cross the Channel, according to an Agence France-Presse tally based on official French and British sources. Official figures cited by the UN refugee agency, the UNHCR, show irregular migration to the EU – notably via Mediterranean sea routes – has plummeted since its peak during the 2015 refugee crisis. Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, will on Monday announce the reopening of a scheme to resettle refugees in the UK as she says “fairness” is at the heart of her vision for the Home Office. It will come as she focuses on safe and legal refugee routes to the UK in her Labour party conference speech. The UK resettlement scheme will reopen immediately, with about a quarter of those admitted to the UK under it expected to be Palestinians and women and girls from Afghanistan. UK government sources said officials were aware of the fatalities. https://www.kyivpost.com/post/89426.text: North America Latin America Europe Eastern Europe Middle East Africa Asia Business Technology Finance Energy Agriculture Reviews EN UK US Elections Trump US Midterms: What Is the Global Impact? In brief: Media commentators across Europe and the Middle East have analyzed the strategic implications of the Democratic Party’s victory in the US midterm elections: what is known about the potential constraints on Donald Trump’s executive authority, the impact on the armed conflict with Iran, military assistance for Ukraine, and technology regulation. by Eurotopics | Nov. 7, 2026, 3:45 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied US President Donald Trump delivers a speech marking the end of the midterm election campaign, at the Lincoln Reflecting Pool in Washington, DC, on Nov. 2, 2026. Photo by MANDEL NGAN / AFP Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip The Democrats’ success in the midterm elections could bring major changes in US foreign policy on issues such as support for Ukraine, the war in Iran and trade policy. Commentators discuss the ramifications for world politics. No telling which way the wind will blow JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . Upping the ante in foreign policy would be risky for a US President Donald Trump – now weakened. As Hürriyet (Turkey) puts in: “A leader may aim to regain the support he has lost at home through military or diplomatic successes abroad. But Trump faces a dilemma, namely that voters are also punishing him for the economic costs of the war with Iran. Consequently, while a new military escalation could restore his image as a strong leader, it could just as easily compound his political defeat... For that reason it is neither correct to say that Trump’s electoral rout will automatically make him more bellicose, nor is it realistic to assume that he will abandon the idea of war altogether... For sometimes it is not a leader’s loss of power that changes the course of history, but his reaction to that loss.” Advertisement Iran’s hand stronger and stronger The election result is a dream come true for Iran, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (Germany) observes: “Trump’s loss of authority is plain for all to see... His endorsement of Pete Hegseth, who he said was doing ‘a very good job’ at the Pentagon, is unlikely to bring any calm to the Republican camp. Many are calling for the secretary of war’s scalp. ... The Iranian regime could not have imagined a more splendid scenario: the vice-president just wants to ‘get out’, the war secretary is on his last legs, and the new Congress is unlikely to grant Trump the additional funds he demands for the war in Iran. Tehran’s hand is getting stronger and stronger while Trump’s options deteriorate.” Other Topics of Interest Zelensky Questions US-Russia Push for New Security Model With Europe At the 9th European Political Community Summit, Zelensky also urged European leaders for deliveries of Patriot and NASAMS interceptors, alongside F-16 ammunition and energy equipment. No to war as a political weapon Italy’s Avvenire comments: Advertisement “One factor of paramount interest to the entire international community following the rejection of Trump’s policies at the ballot box is the indisputable shunning of this US administration’s (external) military adventures and (internal) security policy . Seen in this light, Trump’s defeat is a defeat for war. And not merely because of the economic consequences, however serious they may be for both the United States and the globalized world... We have arrived at the point where war has shamelessly and absurdly been included in the electoral programs in Washington and Tel Aviv alike, as if it were simply one policy among others.” Ukraine not a pawn in US domestic politics Olena Tregub, head of the Independent Anti-Corruption Commission (Nako), warns in Ukrainska Pravda (Ukraine) that efforts to challenge controversial US decisions could make Ukraine the subject of domestic political conflicts: “Already during the first impeachment proceedings against Trump, Ukraine found itself at the centre of the conflict between the president and his political opponents. At the time, one of the issues at stake was the delay in the delivery of US military aid... Should future investigations become nothing more than a tool in the Democrats’ battle against the Republicans, Ukraine once again risks becoming a toxic issue in American politics. We must not allow such a scenario to be repeated. Ukraine should be a cause that unites, not divides.” Advertisement Blow for ethno-nationalism Commentator Lluís Bassets (Spain) is delighted: “Democracy is local, but its effects are also global. The United States has voted overwhelmingly against Trump mainly for domestic reasons... Only issues that affect people’s lives, their pockets and their well-being very directly can explain the scale of this electoral tsunami... The beginning of the end of Trumpism signaled by voters also demonstrates the strength of American democracy. This is perhaps the most powerful global repercussion, in line with the impact of the transfer of power following elections in Hungary, Brazil, Serbia and Israel... This is not a happy day for rampant global far-right ethno-nationalism.” Window of opportunity Europe now has every reason to seek to capitalise on the changes in Washington, Protagon (Greece) emphasises: “Support for Ukraine, security in the eastern Mediterranean and the protection of energy links offer concrete areas for cooperation with the new Congress. The latter’s influence will depend on how far it is prepared to go and on its ability to forge stable cooperative relations with both parties. In short, the US elections have opened a political window of opportunity. European leaders are now called upon to seize this chance through joint decisions, funding and commitments that endure beyond the next election cycle.” Advertisement Don’t underestimate Trump’s influence Europe must remain on guard in the wake of Trump’s defeat, security expert Marco Vicenzino warns in Expresso (Portugal): “The Democratic majority opens up opportunities for Europe to cooperate more closely with Congress. However, it does not dispel the uncertainty over how Trump will balance his commitments to allies, trade policy requirements and his preference for bilateral negotiations... Tuesday’s elections mark the start of a final phase in Trump’s presidency in which he is subject to greater constraints. But to declare him to be finished politically would be to underestimate the power he still wields.” New scenarios for AI Italy’s La Stampa sees implications for Big Tech: “There is a theory that began to circulate immediately after the midterm election results were announced. Namely, that the US election was also a vote on artificial intelligence, on data centres, and on the power of the tech giants to shape US industrial policy. The debacle for the Republicans – who once again had received hundreds of millions of dollars in backing from the tech giants – opens up new scenarios for the future of this technology. Fewer mega-structures, more regulations, more controls.” Advertisement More regulation at home, more chaos abroad In IQ (Lithuania), economist Vytenis Šimkus looks at potential changes in various policy areas: “The technology sector may face tighter regulation. Until now, AI has been developed largely without restrictions. A Democrat-controlled Congress, however, is likely to seek binding rules. These could slow growth while at the same time favouring established market leaders and restricting competition. US presidents whose leeway in domestic affairs is limited by an unfavourable situation in Congress often turn their attention to the international arena and increasingly govern by executive order. As a result, US foreign policy could become even less predictable over the next two years.” Veto right will lead to major confrontations In a Telegram post republished by Echo (Russia), human rights activist Anastasia Burakova examines Trump’s right of veto: “The system of checks and balances in the US is ingeniously designed. Among other things, the president retains the right of veto... Even with a majority in both chambers, the Democrats will by no means always be able to push through their own legislation – to override a presidential veto they need the support of two-thirds of the members of Congress. Over the next two years, I suspect we will witness a serious standoff in which decisions on both sides are blocked, which will affect military aid to Ukraine, US domestic policy and defence spending.” Advertisement See the original here .
